messages.content: Now that the Chicago flights are ticketed, compare the two hotel choices for all four nights, October 19 through 23. I need the complete charges, not just nightly rates, and the Monday trip to the museum loading dock.

The Museum District Hotel is $1,148.72 total, including taxes and fees, for four nights. It is about a seven-minute walk to the loading dock. The Parkside Rail Hotel totals $932.40; Monday morning requires the Blue Line, a transfer to the 66 bus, and a final five-minute walk, about 38 minutes under normal service. The closer hotel costs $216.32 more.
What time would I need to leave Parkside if the case delivery is scheduled for 7:30 Monday morning? Include a reasonable buffer.

I would plan to leave Parkside by 6:35 a.m. That allows roughly 38 minutes in transit plus about 17 minutes for a missed connection or minor delay. From the Museum District Hotel, leaving around 7:10 a.m. would give you time to walk over and report to the dock before 7:30.
That transfer is not appealing with an early delivery. Check late arrival for Sunday at both places. My flight reaches O'Hare at 7:32 p.m., so I may not be at the desk until after 9:00.

The Museum District Hotel has a staffed desk overnight and will hold a guaranteed reservation for late arrival; I can add your flight arrival and an estimated check-in of 9:30 to 10:00 p.m. Parkside's desk closes at 10:00 p.m., but it can arrange lockbox access if you complete online registration by 6:00 p.m. Sunday.
And what are the cancellation terms on the actual rates you priced?

The $1,148.72 Museum District rate can be canceled without penalty until 6:00 p.m. local time on Friday, October 17. After that, the penalty is one night at $267.18 including tax. The $932.40 Parkside rate is refundable until 3:00 p.m. Saturday, October 18; after its deadline, the full stay is nonrefundable.
Morgan is coming with me and we will share one room. What room types are included at the Museum District Hotel?

At that total, the hotel offers either one queen bed or two double beds. A king room is available for $48 more over the stay. All three room types have the same cancellation deadline and late-arrival handling.
One queen is the right choice when the two of us share a room. There is no need to pay extra for the king, and we do not need separate beds.

Understood. The Museum District Hotel with one queen remains $1,148.72 for October 19 through 23. Shall I reserve it for Avery and Morgan Thompson, guarantee it with the card ending in 1842, and add the late-arrival note? The hotel will not charge the card now; payment is collected at checkout unless the cancellation penalty applies.
Before you do, confirm there is no destination fee or separate internet charge missing from that total.

Confirmed. The $1,148.72 includes the room charges, lodging taxes, and the hotel's $18 nightly facility fee. Standard internet is included in that fee. There is no additional destination fee. Parking and incidental purchases would be separate, but neither is included or required for this reservation.
Go ahead and reserve the queen room for both of us. Use the card ending in 1842 as the guarantee, add the late check-in note, and make no charge now.

Reserved at the Museum District Hotel for Avery and Morgan Thompson, October 19-23, four nights, in one queen room. The complete stay total is $1,148.72. The card ending in 1842 guarantees the booking, and no charge was made. The reservation notes your Sunday flight arrival and expected check-in between 9:30 and 10:00 p.m. Free cancellation ends at 6:00 p.m. local time Friday, October 17; afterward, the penalty is $267.18. Confirmation: MDH-819437.
